report.answer_text:
Rubin's "First Look" images came out on June 23, 2025.
What the images showed
Trifid and Lagoon nebulae. The Trifid and Lagoon nebulae (M20 and M8) appear as a vibrant image of glowing gas and scattered stars. One shot was created from 678 individual exposures. It shows two oceans of luminescent gas and dust where stars are born.
Virgo Cluster. Other images show a tiny portion of Rubin's view of the Virgo Cluster, a zoo of galaxies. They include big, bright, fuzzy ellipticals, delicate spirals and tiny dwarfs. Many of the smaller galaxies in the frame are distant background objects, not cluster members.
Wide-field views and videos. Additional images and videos showing the "dynamic universe" were released on June 23 as well. The images were meant to show Rubin's enormous field of view and its opening of the time domain. That means repeatedly imaging the sky to catch things that change.
The survey it's carrying out
Rubin is carrying out the Legacy Survey of Space and Time (LSST), a landmark 10-year campaign to map the southern sky with the world's largest digital camera. Science News reported that the observatory will begin the 10-year survey of the southern sky in late 2025. National Geographic noted the observatory is expected to discover 20 billion new galaxies over the next decade. The survey's science goals include dark matter and dark energy.
